To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the secrecy capacity of the delay limited fading channel is zero if only main channel CSI is available at the transmitter, and (ii) the secrecy capacity is strictly positive if both main and eavesdrop- ter channel CSI are available.
the secrecy outage phenomenon can be overcome by a novel two-stage approach and the secure delay limited rate is non-zero under the assumption that only the main channel is known at the transmitter.

the delay limited secrecy rate of a flat fading channel can be non-zero even when the transmitter does not know the eavesdropper CSI and can be made arbitrarily close to the secrecy capacity when the transmitter has perfect knowledge of both the eavesdropping channel and the main channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the secrecy rate of the flat fading Gaussian wiretap channel under delay constraints, which has not been addressed in the literature.
the problem of secrecy communication over flat fading channels under a strict delay requirement.
the secrecy capacity of the delay limited fading channel under two different assumptions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the secrecy capacity is non-zero for a large class of channel distributions, under the assumptions of either perfect or imperfect CSI at the transmitter.
the delay limited secrecy rate is non-zero under a wide class of fading distributions and for any delay constraint (for both cases).
, in contrast to the delay free case, the secrecy capacity of the delay limited fading channel is strictly positive for a wide class of fading distributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish the existence of a non-zero secure rate under a strict delay and secrecy outage constraint for the flat fading channel.
the secrecy capacity of the delay limited fading channel can be non-zero even if the CSI of the eavesdropper is not available at the transmitter.
we have provided a complete characterization of the secure rate region of the delay limited channel under the two different assumptions on transmitter channel CSI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in both scenarios, the secure rate is non-zero and is a strictly positive fraction of the delay limited capacity.
, in the high SNR regime, the secrecy capacity of flat fading channels can be made arbitrarily close to the capacity of the same channel without secrecy constraints.
the secrecy capacity can be non-zero even under a strict delay requirement and without requiring any additional CSI at the transmitter.
